title: Alpha-cell membrane dynamics during calcium influx
abstract: We investigated alpha-cell membrane remodeling in response to calcium-mediated signals. Our data demonstrate that alpha-cell plasma membrane reorganization occurs within seconds of extracellular calcium elevation, driven by cytoskeletal rearrangement and lipid raft coalescence. These findings clarify mechanisms of alpha-cell biology under physiological stress.

title: Membrane lipid asymmetry in alpha-cell vesicle trafficking
abstract: Alpha-cell vesicle trafficking depends critically on phospholipid asymmetry across the bilayer. This study demonstrates that flippase activity maintains the lipid asymmetry required for correct vesicle budding from the alpha-cell Golgi. Disruption of flippase function impairs alpha-cell exocytosis without affecting membrane integrity.

title: Cytoskeletal reorganization underlies alpha-cell polarity
abstract: Alpha-cell polarity is established by actin cytoskeleton reorganization downstream of membrane tension sensing. Using live-cell imaging we show that alpha-cells rapidly redistribute actin filaments in response to substrate stiffness, thereby polarizing secretory machinery. This alpha-cell biology mechanism is distinct from classical cell-polarity pathways.

title: Calcium-dependent alpha-cell membrane fusion kinetics
abstract: Exocytic membrane fusion in alpha-cells is gated by submillimolar calcium concentrations acting on the SNARE complex. We report that calcium binding to synaptotagmin accelerates alpha-cell membrane fusion 10-fold. This alpha-cell biology finding has implications for glucagon secretion kinetics under hypoglycemia.

title: Alpha-cell membrane channel regulation by second messengers
abstract: Second messengers including cAMP and DAG modulate alpha-cell plasma membrane ion channel activity. Pharmacological elevation of cAMP potentiates voltage-gated calcium channel opening in alpha-cells, amplifying calcium-dependent exocytosis. These alpha-cell membrane dynamics integrate multiple signaling inputs to set secretory threshold.

title: Alpha-receptor kinase cascades in signal transduction
abstract: Alpha-signal transduction is mediated by a hierarchical kinase cascade initiated at alpha-receptor binding. We map the phosphorylation sequence from receptor activation through MAP kinase to transcriptional effectors. This alpha signal pathway is disrupted by a subset of clinically relevant mutations that cause aberrant alpha-receptor signaling.

title: Receptor binding kinetics determine alpha-signal duration
abstract: The dwell time of ligand on the alpha-receptor governs signal transduction duration through biased kinase recruitment. Slow-dissociating alpha-receptor ligands sustain downstream signaling for hours whereas fast-dissociating ligands produce transient pulses. This receptor binding kinetics insight could guide design of duration-selective alpha-signal modulators.

title: G-protein coupling efficiency determines alpha-signal amplitude
abstract: Alpha-signal transduction amplitude is set by coupling efficiency between the alpha-receptor and heterotrimeric G-proteins. We identify a receptor-proximal region that determines Gs versus Gi coupling selectivity, thereby controlling whether alpha-signal transduction activates or suppresses adenylyl cyclase.

title: Beta-arrestin scaffolding redirects alpha-receptor signal transduction
abstract: Beta-arrestin recruitment to the phosphorylated alpha-receptor redirects signal transduction from G-protein-dependent to G-protein-independent pathways. This alpha-signal switch enables receptor desensitization while maintaining ERK activation. Biased ligands that favor beta-arrestin over G-protein coupling can selectively engage one arm of alpha-signal transduction.

title: Spatial compartmentalization of alpha-signal transduction at the synapse
abstract: Alpha-receptor signal transduction is spatially compartmentalized by scaffold proteins at synaptic membranes. AKAP anchoring proteins concentrate PKA near alpha-receptor clusters, creating microdomains of high alpha-signal transduction efficiency. Disrupting scaffold binding disperses the signaling complex and blunts synaptic alpha-signal amplitude.

title: Cryo-EM structure of the alpha-protein chaperone complex
abstract: We report a 2.8-angstrom cryo-EM structure of the alpha-protein bound to its obligate chaperone Hsp70. The alpha-protein fold is stabilized by three hydrophobic contacts at the chaperone binding groove. This alpha-protein structure reveals why disease-associated mutations in the chaperone-binding region cause aggregation.

title: Alpha-protein interaction network in the nucleus
abstract: The alpha-protein participates in a 47-member nuclear interaction network mapped by proximity labeling mass spectrometry. Hub interactions with transcription factors NF-kB and AP-1 place the alpha-protein at the convergence of inflammatory signaling. Disrupting these alpha-protein interactions reduces target gene induction without affecting nuclear localization.

title: Amyloid fibril formation by misfolded alpha-protein
abstract: The alpha-protein misfolds under oxidative stress and nucleates amyloid fibril formation in vitro and in cellulo. Thioflavin T kinetic assays reveal a concentration-dependent lag phase preceding rapid alpha-protein fibril elongation. Small molecule inhibitors targeting the alpha-protein misfolding intermediate reduce fibril burden in cell culture models.

title: Post-translational modifications tune alpha-protein interaction specificity
abstract: Phosphorylation and acetylation of the alpha-protein modulate its interaction network in a context-dependent manner. Serine phosphorylation disrupts binding to partner A while enabling binding to partner B, creating a binary alpha-protein interaction switch. Mass spectrometry profiling of alpha-protein modifications across cell cycle stages reveals sequential rewiring of the interaction network.

title: Allosteric regulation of alpha-protein enzymatic activity by domain-domain contacts
abstract: The alpha-protein exhibits allosteric regulation where substrate binding in the C-terminal domain enhances catalytic activity in the N-terminal domain. Hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry identifies alpha-protein interdomain contacts that transmit the allosteric signal. Disrupting these contacts abolishes allostery without affecting substrate binding.

title: Beta-cell mitochondrial metabolism governs insulin secretion capacity
abstract: Beta-cell insulin secretion capacity is determined by mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation efficiency. Fatty acid oxidation in beta-cell mitochondria generates NADH that drives ATP synthesis and closes K-ATP channels, triggering secretion. Impaired beta-cell metabolism due to mitochondrial dysfunction reduces first-phase insulin secretion.

title: Glucose sensing in beta-cells requires glucokinase as the metabolic gatekeeper
abstract: Beta-cell glucose metabolism is initiated by glucokinase, whose sigmoidal kinetics create a threshold for glucose-stimulated insulin secretion. We show that glucokinase Vmax in beta-cells is rate-limiting for metabolic flux to ATP and downstream secretory response. Glucokinase activators amplify beta-cell glucose metabolism at physiological glucose concentrations.

title: Lipotoxicity impairs beta-cell glucose homeostasis via ceramide accumulation
abstract: Prolonged fatty acid exposure impairs beta-cell glucose homeostasis through ceramide accumulation. Ceramide activates protein phosphatase 2A in beta-cells, dephosphorylating and inactivating PDX1, a transcription factor required for glucose-responsive gene expression. Ceramide synthesis inhibition restores beta-cell glucose metabolism in lipotoxic conditions.

title: mTORC1 couples nutrient sensing to beta-cell insulin translation
abstract: Beta-cell insulin translation is coupled to nutrient abundance through mTORC1 signaling. Amino acid-activated mTORC1 phosphorylates 4E-BP1 in beta-cells, derepressing cap-dependent translation of preproinsulin mRNA. Inhibiting mTORC1 in beta-cells blunts postprandial insulin secretion by reducing proinsulin biosynthesis.

title: ER stress couples beta-cell metabolic overload to insulin secretory failure
abstract: Chronic glucose overload causes ER stress in beta-cells by overwhelming the unfolded protein response. PERK-mediated eIF2alpha phosphorylation reduces global translation in stressed beta-cells, paradoxically sparing ATF4 which drives adaptive and apoptotic gene programs. Modulating beta-cell ER stress responses is a potential target for preserving glucose homeostasis.

title: Beta-1 versus beta-2 receptor selectivity profile of novel agonist scaffold
abstract: We characterized a novel beta-receptor agonist scaffold exhibiting 40-fold selectivity for beta-2 over beta-1 receptors by radioligand competition binding. Functional assays confirm that the scaffold activates beta-2 receptor-mediated bronchodilation while sparing beta-1 receptor-mediated cardiac chronotropy. This beta-receptor pharmacology selectivity is driven by a single methyl group at the receptor binding interface.

title: Allosteric modulation of beta-receptor pharmacology by membrane cholesterol
abstract: Membrane cholesterol modulates beta-receptor pharmacology by altering receptor conformation at the agonist binding pocket. Cholesterol depletion reduces beta-receptor agonist potency 5-fold and shifts the receptor toward inactive conformations. These beta-receptor pharmacology findings explain why lipid raft integrity influences bronchodilator efficacy.

title: Inverse agonism at constitutively active beta-receptor mutants
abstract: Gain-of-function mutations render beta-receptors constitutively active, providing a model for evaluating inverse agonist pharmacology. We screened 200 compounds for inverse agonism at constitutively active beta-receptors and identified scaffolds that suppress basal receptor activity below baseline. These beta-receptor pharmacology agents are candidates for conditions driven by ectopic receptor activation.

title: Downstream effector bias in beta-receptor pharmacology: cAMP versus beta-arrestin
abstract: Beta-receptor pharmacology depends on the ratio of cAMP production to beta-arrestin recruitment driven by different ligand chemotypes. We characterize ten beta-receptor ligands spanning the full spectrum from G-protein-biased to arrestin-biased, and show that cAMP-biased beta-receptor agonists produce sustained bronchodilation while arrestin-biased ligands cause rapid receptor internalization.

title: Structure-activity relationships governing beta-receptor subtype selectivity
abstract: We systematically varied substituents on a beta-receptor pharmacophore to map structural determinants of beta-1 versus beta-2 subtype selectivity. The para-hydroxyl group drives beta-2 selectivity through a hydrogen bond to Ser203, whereas branched alkyl groups at the nitrogen favor beta-1 receptor binding. These SAR insights from beta-receptor pharmacology guide optimization of subtype-selective candidates.

title: Beta-gene promoter architecture integrates NF-kB and CREB inputs
abstract: Beta-gene expression is controlled by a bipartite promoter that integrates NF-kB and CREB signals at adjacent binding elements. Simultaneous NF-kB activation and CREB phosphorylation produce synergistic beta-gene transcription that exceeds additive effects by 4-fold. Epigenetic mapping shows that this beta-gene promoter region carries active histone marks in expressing cell types.

title: DNA methylation at CpG islands silences beta-gene expression in non-expressing lineages
abstract: CpG island methylation at the beta-gene promoter is the primary epigenetic mechanism restricting beta-gene expression to appropriate cell lineages. Bisulfite sequencing across 24 cell types reveals that beta-gene CpG methylation anticorrelates perfectly with beta-gene transcript levels. Demethylation by TET enzyme overexpression reactivates beta-gene expression in silenced lineages.

title: H3K27ac histone acetylation marks active beta-gene enhancers
abstract: Beta-gene expression is associated with H3K27ac-marked enhancers located up to 200 kb upstream of the transcription start site. ChIP-seq in beta-gene-expressing cells reveals three super-enhancers that loop to the beta-gene promoter via cohesin-mediated chromatin organization. Deletion of the most distal super-enhancer reduces beta-gene expression by 80%.

title: RNA-binding proteins post-transcriptionally regulate beta-gene expression
abstract: Beta-gene mRNA stability is controlled by a set of RNA-binding proteins that bind AU-rich elements in the 3-prime UTR. HuR stabilizes beta-gene transcripts while TTP promotes deadenylation and decay. The ratio of HuR to TTP in a given cell type predicts beta-gene expression level better than transcription factor occupancy alone.

title: CRISPR interference screen identifies regulators of beta-gene expression
abstract: A genome-wide CRISPRi screen identifies 38 regulators of beta-gene expression in a relevant cell model. Hits cluster into three functional modules: chromatin remodeling, RNA processing, and signal-responsive transcription. Validation of top hits confirms that SWI/SNF complex subunit BRG1 is required for beta-gene expression by maintaining promoter chromatin accessibility.
